target_paper.title: MedXpertQA: Benchmarking Expert-Level Medical Reasoning and Understanding
target_paper.original_source: Table 5 (LLMs on MedXpertQA Text), the two rows marked as a sampled subset: o1 46.24/39.66/44.67 and o3-mini 37.63/36.21/37.30 on the 244-item seed-42 10% sample; Expert (Pre-Licensed) 41.74/45.44/42.60 on the full Text set

generation.parameters: zero-shot CoT, 2 stages per item; no system message and no temperature for o1/o3-mini (paper C.2, api_agent.py); max_completion_tokens 8192; seed = seed_idx (0 = the original)
generation.battery: Text sampled subset, 244 items x 2 stages x 1 seed (o1) / 3 seeds (o3-mini) = 1928 archived calls; median over seeds per item; item-level bootstrap 2000 draws (rng 20260907); parser/scorer imported from the repo

results.judged_by: automatic rule per ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 as the card instantiates it (median over seeds inside the binomial 95% band of the printed value; o1 > o3-mini; o1 > the 42.60 expert baseline); the paper reports no significance test for these rows, so that clause is vacuous; human double-coding pending
results.note: Text subset only (MM not run). Per-item file items.jsonl carries ids, hashes and parsed letters; calls.jsonl carries the model replies with the question text redacted (prompt_sha256 kept) under the authors' Appendix A request.

deviations_from_card: o1 runs 1 seed instead of the card's 3 (the card's own cheaper alternative; ANALYSIS_PLAN section 3 asks for 3) - the o1 row therefore has no run-to-run spread
no prompt-paraphrase arm (ANALYSIS_PLAN section 3): the claim is a benchmark level under the paper's exact prompt
MM subset not run, so Table 4's o1 56.28 is not checked
per-paper cap USD 60 instead of the card's est_cost_usd 134 (which assumed 3 seeds for both arms)
the o3-mini row is judged as a second claim row inside this card rather than as a separate card
reproducibility_frictions_observed: per-question original outputs are not published (only leaderboard aggregates), so only aggregate accuracy is comparable; no item-level agreement with the original run can be computed
paper Appendix A asks that no example be shared online, so this card's L1 archive stores item ids, hashes and model replies but not the question text (see LOG POLICY)

the Expert (Pre-Licensed) row of Table 5 (42.60) is computed on the FULL Text set from aggregated examinee response distributions - it is not an integer item count and not the 244-item sample - yet the card's judgment compares o1's sampled accuracy against it directly

eval/model/api_agent.py hard-codes an OpenAI-compatible proxy (api_key '[API_KEY]', base_url '[BASE_URL]'), so the published numbers were produced through a proxy of unknown routing; this re-run posts to api.openai.com directly

the original run is a single pass (seed=0) and o-series ignore temperature, so the paper's own run-to-run spread is unknown; the seed parameter is sent as the original did, but OpenAI documents it as best-effort and reasoning models are not deterministic
main.py's --temperature default of 0 is silently dropped for o1/o3-mini by api_agent.py; 'greedy decoding' in section 4.1 therefore does not apply to these two rows
the repo sends the stage-1 user turn as a content-parts list even for text-only items; replicated here verbatim, but it cannot be exercised offline
the sampled subsets ship in the repo without the seed-42 sampling script, so the 10% draw itself is not reproducible - it is taken as given (186/1861 and 58/589 of the full Text set)

utils.answer_cleansing extracts the FIRST case-sensitive \b[A-J]\b of the stage-2 reply, so the English words 'A' and 'I' are read as options A and I (a first-person refusal scores as I), while a lower-case letter yields no prediction at all (scored incorrect). Kept as released - it is the parser that produced Tables 4 and 5.
